newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hopes for U.N. Zaire mandate within hours.
newsitem.headline: France hopes for U.N. Zaire mandate within hours.

text.p: France said on Tuesday it hoped the United Nations would be in a position to approve within hours a mandate for a humanitarian force to bring relief to starving refugees in eastern Zaire.

Foreign Minister Herve de Charette told parliament: "I hope we will have the answers we are waiting for in the coming hours so that the Security Council will finally be able to meet and take the necessary decision."

The minister said he could not disagree with the impatience voiced by parliamentary questioners about the slow reaction of the international community to the plight of one million Hutu refugees displaced by fighting, but he said: "As we speak, things are moving forward and I believe progressing fast. It's about time, but I think it is the case."
De Charette early spoke by telephone to Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy and French officials said they had agreed that a Canadian would lead in the proposed U.N. force in eastern Zaire.
He told parliament that U.S. participation is the operation was indispensible "because everyone must take responsibility in the international community".
The newspaper Le Monde quoted sources in the United States as saying Washington had agreed to participate in the relief action and up to 1,000 American troops would be involved.
